किं—नर m. ‘what sort of man?’ a mythical being with a human figure and the head of a horse (or with a horse's body and the head of a man, Śiś. iv, 38; originally perhaps a kind of monkey, cf. वा-नर; in later times (like the Naras) reckoned among the Gandharvas or celestial choristers, and celebrated as musicians; also attached to the service of Kubera; (with Jains) one of the eight orders of the Vyantaras), Mn.; MBh. &c.
N. of a prince, VP.
of Nara (a son of Vibhīṣaṇa), Rājat. i, 197

N. of a locality g. तक्षशिलादि

(perhaps = कीना॑श) a cultivator of the soil [‘a vile man’, Sāy.] RV. x, 106, 10.
See s.v. कि॑म्.
